definition: A function is increasing on an interval if its output gets bigger as $x$ gets bigger there, so $a < b$ gives $f(a) < f(b)$; this holds whenever $f'(x) > 0$ for every $x$ in the interval.
A function is decreasing on an interval if its output gets smaller as $x$ gets bigger there, so $a < b$ gives $f(a) > f(b)$; this holds whenever $f'(x) < 0$ for every $x$ in the interval.
A point on a curve where $f'(x) = 0$, so the tangent is horizontal; it may be a local maximum, a local minimum or neither.
